summary: Intermittent 5xx surge after ingress throttle oscillation causes runtime crashloop for heavy streaming tenants
description:
Issue summary: BrightAssist (dedicated tenant) reported a sharp increase in 5xx responses starting ~2026-03-12T21:10 UTC. Errors correlate with a series of short-lived ingress throttle oscillations during an evening traffic ramp. Upstream serving-runtime instances entered crash/restart loops for streaming sessions, amplifying the 5xx wave.

Impact: Intermittent 50-70% request error rate on the customer streaming route (/v1/stream) for ~40 minutes; customer reported degraded real-time UX and multiple failed sessions. No data loss reported; failures are request-level 502/503/504.

Environment: prod us-west, dedicated capacity pool (dedicated-gpu-pool-04) serving redwood-13b-v1 pinned variant. API gateway fronted by edge fleet us-west-1.

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) Customer sends sustained streaming connections with long-lived sessions (30-120s) and many small incremental messages.
2) Ingress rate limiter detects per-tenant burst pattern and engages adaptive token-bucket throttle.
3) Throttle parameters oscillate (fast tighten -> release) as autoscaler and the gateway's reconnects change instantaneous load.
4) Some serving-runtime pods experience increasing connection churn and enter crash/restart cycles (OOMs or watchdog-triggered restarts) causing upstream 5xx propagation.

Observed behavior:
- Sudden spikes of 502 and 503 from api-gateway, with a tail of 504s while retries queued.
- Runtime logs show repeated watchdog restarts for streaming worker threads and accelerated GC around the same windows.
- Autoscaler observed short bursts of scale-up then immediate scale-down causing preemption pressure on ephemeral instances.

Expected behavior:
- Stable throttle behavior (no oscillation) with graceful shed/queueing and autoscaler ramp smoothness.
- No crashloops on serving-runtime for bounded streaming workloads.

Relevant logs & dashboards:
- Grafana panel: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/ingress/ingress-throttle-overview?orgId=1&var-region=us-west
- Runtime pod logs (sample): https://kibana.redwood.ai/app/discover#/doc/serving-runtime-logs?id=pod-cc12f
- Support Slack thread: https://slack.redwood.ai/archives/C03SUPPORT/p1646983200

Notes: Initial mitigation applied (see comments) to stabilize customer traffic; engineering investigating root cause and providing patch for throttle state machine and runtime resilience.

investigation_notes: Ingress metrics show token-bucket refill oscillation correlated with short autoscaler pulses — likely feedback loop between gateway per-tenant throttle and autoscaler-driven capacity changes.
Runtime logs show repeated 'watchdog timeout: streaming-worker' preceding pod restarts; memory usage climbed then dropped before restart (pattern of fragmentation or leak over long-lived sessions).
A small percentage of connections exhibited repeated hedged retries from the client which exacerbated load and pushed ephemeral workers into busy-wait on reclaim path.
Reproducer: synthetic client that opens 100 long-lived streams with small heartbeats reproduces throttle oscillation locally on a staging replica when combined with a quick scale-down trigger.

Hypothesis: adaptive throttle reduces tokens aggressively on bursts; autoscaler interprets reduced throughput as low utilization and scales down, which then causes a surge on reconnect — creating a cycle. The runtime streaming cleanup path doesn't handle abrupt connection churn well, causing watchdog restarts.
Linked PR for observability tweak: adding token-bucket state export to Grafana (PR referenced above) to validate oscillation mitigation during canary.
next_steps: 1) Deploy throttle-state machine patch that adds minimum hold-time before parameter adjustments (canary 2026-03-13 11:00 UTC).
2) Deploy runtime defensive fix for streaming worker cleanup and increase watchdog thresholds for canary pool.
3) Coordinate with customer to temporarily limit concurrent streams during canary (BrightAssist agreed).
4) Monitor Grafana for token-bucket oscillation and runtime restart rate for 2h post-canary; if stable, schedule full roll on 2026-03-14.
5) Postmortem to be drafted on Confluence linking metrics and mitigation steps.
resolution: Mitigation in progress: temporary throttle pin applied and customer traffic reduced. Canary patch scheduled. Final root cause pending post-canary verification.
